scope.summary: Add the first Rust-owned project-hook pattern: a main-checkout guard that denies high-risk mutating Git commands in the canonical checkout while allowing worktree and read-only operations.
explicit_non_claims: No production branch protection, external infrastructure, credentials, or remote required status context is changed.
The shell shim is irreducible hook glue only; policy remains in Rust.
The guard is a project-hook admission guard for direct Bash tool commands, not a complete shell sandbox for arbitrarily nested shell interpreters.
Generated JSON faces are materialized by infra/ci/materialize-cloud-ci-generated-faces.sh, not hand edited.

planning_decision.required_self_serve_step: Attempted fable/ralplan planning through Claude twice; both invocations produced no output before timeout, so a repo-local fallback plan was recorded under ignored .omc/plans.
planning_decision.chosen_pattern: Rust binary at tools/oya-checkout-guard-app with a minimal tools/hooks/main-checkout-guard.sh exec shim that fails open with a warning if tools/hooks/bin/oya-checkout-guard is absent.
planning_decision.reason: Keeps policy testable and side-effect-free in Rust while satisfying current Claude/Codex hook APIs, which execute configured command strings.

facets.F1_correctness: The pure decision kernel denies checkout/switch/reset --hard/clean -f*/rebase/non-ff merge/non-ff pull/stash pop/apply in the canonical checkout and allows read-only, ff-only, worktree-management, branch-delete, push, and outside-canonical invocations.
facets.F2_tests: TDD red/green covered initial deny-list behavior plus recovery regressions for command prefixes, shell builtin option/terminator forms, combined exec short-option clusters, global options, Git target env vars, path-qualified git/env, env -S direct/wrapper/attached forms, env -P/-v/-u attached forms, attached exec -aNAME, dynamic target paths, canonical git-dir ordering, shell wrappers, shell redirections, git aliases including shell/config-env/GIT_CONFIG_COUNT aliases, embedded non-shell alias arguments, process-env-backed --config-env aliases, function wrappers, subshell cwd scope, command substitutions, brace/control groups, ff-only option conflicts, and pushd/popd behavior.
facets.F3_maintainability: The shell shim contains only repo-root discovery and exec/fail-open bootstrap handling; all policy lives in a small Rust library with focused unit tests.
facets.F4_compatibility: Existing hook wiring is preserved and mirrored in both Claude and Codex configs; enforcement-liveness census and generated faces are settled.
facets.F5_security: Production Rust uses forbid(unsafe_code) and contains no unwrap/expect/panic matches; deny reasons name the worktree policy and FRIC-022/FRIC-1781062867.
facets.F6_privacy: The hook consumes local hook command JSON and paths only; no tenant or personal data processing is introduced.
facets.F7_operability: The missing-binary path exits 0 with a stderr warning naming the Buck2 --out command; runtime deny exits 2 with a one-line reason.
facets.F8_performance: Warm shim+binary latency measured at 0.21s for 20 invocations after process-env alias hardening, about 10.5 ms each, under the 100 ms budget.
facets.F9_compliance: ADR-0523 irreducible-glue ledger now authorizes this hook shim row; serde_json usage is covered in registry/dependency-rationales.json.
facets.F10_reversibility: Rollback is a normal git revert of the additive crate, shim, hook wiring, metadata, generated faces, and evidence.
facets.F11_observability: Gate tests print hook/command/stub corpus counts, and the guard emits explicit warning/deny stderr messages for bootstrap and policy outcomes.
facets.F13_migration: Establishes a reusable Rust-hook pattern without expanding shell policy logic or adding new dependencies.
